correctness.rationale: Normalized orthogonality gives the squared norm of the triple convolution. The triangle inequality reduces the maximum to magnitudes. The antipodal RMS operation increases each nonnegative autocorrelation by Cauchy–Schwarz and preserves R₀=M. If it changes an unequal pair, the sum of magnitudes strictly increases, so some nonzero R_h increases and the (h,−h,0) term in the autocorrelation cube increases strictly. For balanced magnitudes, independently expand the three antipodal Laurent binomials. Since v₂=v₁+v₃, surviving signed exponents are (k,−k,k), so all three pair degrees have the same parity, hence are all even in degree six. Up to permutation the patterns (6,0,0),(4,2,0),(2,2,2) contribute respectively 20, 15·6·2=180 and 90·(8+1+1)=900. This yields 20s³+120s e₂+420e₃, with M=2s; the two sharp symmetric-polynomial bounds force X=Y=Z, and give moment ratio 85/9. With all magnitudes equal, alignment in each fiber v_j makes the antipodal products common. Factoring their square root λ, the zero-sum triangles force (η₁η₃/η₂)²=1, and the sign choice of λ removes the minus branch. The basis v₁,v₃ therefore gives exactly the scalar character family, which attains equality. Differences of root vertices generate the lattice, so the projective character parameters are unique. At N≥7 there is no aliasing between triple sums in [−3,3]²; no Nth-root restriction on phases is needed. At N=6 the only distinct collisions are the three opposite-vertex pairs at the six extreme triple sums (each a singleton), adding 6 to 2040 and giving the strict lower witness 341/36. No optimal norm at smaller grids is inferred. The independent enumeration in /workspace/branches/30df5558-c964-4978-ade3-1ca8f5928351/record3-independent-check.txt agrees on all 37 fibers, the polynomial, and the residue counts. Frozen checker.py and checker_output.txt were inspected, not executed; python3 checker.py is the packaged replay. The global inequalities, not the finite test arrays, establish optimality.
